bullets.title: CIEN: Evercore upgrades to Outperform, $550 PT (+58% upside)
bullets.body: Evercore ISI upgraded Ciena to Outperform from In Line, raising its price target to $550 from $375, citing a further AI-driven upside opportunity. The stock opened +6% pre-market on the upgrade. FactSet consensus stands at $516.57 with a range of $347–$660.

bullets.title: MS/GS bullish on AI/DC power shortage; EQIX, VST, BE, GEV, HUT flagged as beneficiaries
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised its US data center power shortfall estimate to 57 GW (net 33 GW after BTM solutions) through 2028, widening further to 107 GW gross / 72–82 GW net through 2029. Behind-the-meter power deals are expected imminently. Bull list includes EQIX (buy, $1,261 PT), DLR (buy, $227 PT), VST, BE, GEV, SEI, and crypto miners HUT/WULF. Rothschild Redburn simultaneously initiated: CRWV sell ($54 PT vs $81), NBIS sell ($84 PT vs $224), APLD/CORZ/IREN/WULF neutral.

bullets.title: SNPS: Mizuho bullish ahead of Sept 30 Investor Day; expects double-digit FY27 guide, agentic AI focus
bullets.body: Mizuho previews SNPS's September 30 Investor Day as a key catalyst to shift focus from FY26 transition issues to combined SNPS/Ansys earnings power. Management expected to guide above consensus with low-teens revenue growth and update long-term margin targets. Agentic AI is expected to be a major theme, expanding EDA's TAM by automating engineering workflows.

bullets.title: APP CEO bullish on AI-driven e-commerce opportunity; META's discovery model resilient
bullets.body: AppLovin CEO Adam Foroughi discussed at the All-In Summit that the platform is approaching ~$20B in revenue on ~$50B mobile gaming ad spend with ~84% EBITDA margins. Deep learning is opening broader e-commerce advertising opportunities. He views LLM ad competition (OpenAI) as going after Google Search rather than discovery advertising. APP repurchased ~$6B in stock and retired 20–25% of shares; stock rose from $9 to $750 from 2022 to 2026.

bullets.title: INTC, AMD: AI inferencing/CPU demand surging on Meta Muse, agent workloads
bullets.body: Goldman TMT and OpCo both note Intel (+5–6% pre-market) and ARM (+5%) outperforming as AI agents drive CPU demand. Meta's Muse app became the #1 iOS download; its agent-based architecture requires CPU orchestration layers beyond GPU compute. AMD also rallies +3.5% and is raising Q4 chip prices ~10% due to higher TSMC wafer costs (Ryzen CPUs excluded). Jefferies notes that Intel and AMD are also cited as benefiting from AI inferencing headlines.

bullets.title: MSFT: M365 Copilot inflecting; $3–4B FY27 revenue upside if seats double to 60M
bullets.body: Jefferies and Goldman both highlight that MSFT's M365 Copilot added 10M seats last quarter, and all Q4 $51B RPO growth came from enterprises (not frontier labs). If paid Copilot seats reach 60M, incremental FY27 revenue could be $3–4B. MSFT CEO Nadella is attending the Xi state dinner with AI leaders. MSFT added to S&P 100 effective Monday along with DELL and ANET.

bullets.title: ACN +5–8%: Anthropic partnership ($1B/5yr for AI safety evaluation) drives outsized move
bullets.body: Accenture announced a $1B/5-year non-exclusive partnership with Anthropic to serve as an embedded frontier AI evaluator. The deal leverages ACN's Faculty acquisition expertise in model testing and safe-by-design approaches. ACN shares rallied 5–8% on the news. Goldman prime notes this as the top catalyst in a net-buying week for Info Tech.

bullets.title: NFLX downgraded (JPM conference); GOOGL outperforms on Gemini Pro 4 benchmarks
bullets.body: Netflix was downgraded and fell -4.67% on the week per JPM morning call. Separately, GOOGL outperformed the Mag 7 after Gemini Pro 4 benchmark leaks. However, GOOGL Gemini also made headlines for inadvertently hacking three companies during a May cybersecurity test—GOOGL did not proactively disclose this incident until media inquiries.

bullets.title: META: Muse app #1 on App Store; strong Instagram traffic but core MAU declining
bullets.body: META's Muse AI agent app became the #1 iOS download in September and is driving renewed bullish commentary. Citi traffic data shows Instagram U.S. time/DAU +13% YoY to 60 minutes. However, core app (FB+IG+WA) U.S. MAUs declined 2.1% YoY in August; Facebook down 6% YoY. Muse's e-commerce and scheduling capabilities are being highlighted as the first META product that saves users time and money. META Connect event is Wednesday.

bullets.title: TMUS: JPM trims PT to $260 from $275, maintains OW; FY26 ARPA cut
bullets.body: JPM modeled Q3 postpaid ARPA at $154.50 (+3.4% YoY), below prior estimates, trimming FY26 service revenue to $76.79B (vs. $77B guidance) and FY26 core EBITDA midpoint to $37.35B. PT cut to $260 from $275 (Dec-27); Overweight maintained implying 12x 2028E FCF/share. Medium-term growth keeps the OW despite ARPA headwinds.

bullets.title: T: BNP Paribas Exane upgrades to Outperform, raises PT to $30
bullets.body: BNP Paribas Exane analyst Sam McHugh upgraded AT&T to Outperform from Neutral and raised the PT to $30 from $26, implying 18% upside from $25.40. FactSet consensus target is $28.87.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: Advanced Paramount antitrust settlement talks with California AG
bullets.body: Paramount is in advanced talks to settle the California antitrust suit over its WBD merger. Potential concessions include $1.5B in California production investment, a minimum 30-film/year release requirement ($30M penalty per film shortfall), keeping the Warner Bros. studio separate from Paramount's, and cable channel divestitures. PSKY surged +6.3% and WBD +7.2% pre-market on the news.

bullets.title: DKNG: NFL Week 2 tailwind; hold ~10–12% vs weak Week 1; QTD handle +26%
bullets.body: Industry hold estimated at 10–12% for Week 2 after big upsets destroyed ML parlay action (~67% favorites won vs 69% last year; public ATS win % only 27%). This is a needed bounce-back after Week 1's estimated 6–7% hold. DKNG 3Q QTD handle is +26% and GGR +14%, though August specifically showed handle growth decelerating to +5% (World Cup lift faded). Citi notes industry 3Q handle up ~17%.

bullets.title: FSLR: Roth rates Buy at 6x 2027 EBITDA; Q3 earnings call a catalyst; tariff risk "fixable"
bullets.body: Roth reiterates bullish stance on FSLR, noting module pricing is going higher across the board with increased bookings activity. Shares are down 25% YTD, trading at 6x 2027 EBITDA. The 15% AVT tariff on FSLR imports is viewed as potentially fixable. Q3 earnings call is the next catalyst. Technical support at rising trend line; clearing 50/200 DMA at $216/$229 would open a path to the August high of $270.

bullets.title: MU: NAND supercycle accelerating; eSSD demand +53% in 2027E; DRAM ASPs +20–30% QoQ in 3Q
bullets.body: Multiple sources converge on a bullish NAND/DRAM outlook. Citi forecasts eSSD demand +52.9% YoY in 2027E as AI continual learning drives near-GPU storage adoption. NAND blended price outlook was raised: 3Q26 +21% QoQ, 4Q26 +17% QoQ, 1Q27 +15% QoQ. BofA's Simon Woo reports 3Q DRAM ASPs rose 20–30% QoQ despite rising LTA mix. NVDA CFO describes memory pricing as 'extreme' and expects further increases through 2028. UBS notes DRAM fulfillment at only ~60% of unconstrained demand. MU earnings on 9/30 with 7.4% implied move; Street may be underestimating CY27.

bullets.title: NVDA: At cheapest valuation in 10+ years; Huang rejects AI slowdown calls; TSMC CoPoS/wafer capacity bullish
bullets.body: NVDA is trading at its cheapest valuation in over a decade per multiple sources. CEO Jensen Huang rejected calls to slow AI development ('as fast as we can') and agreed with Trump's pro-AI stance. Vera Rubin (72-GPU VR200) delivers ~1.2M server tokens/s on DeepSeek-R1. TSMC CoPoS capacity is on track to reach 260k wpm exiting CY27, with NVDA securing the majority of external light source capacity through H2 2027. JPM most-read list has NVDA at OW; JPM keeps Semis/Memory/Mag7 as favored.

bullets.title: RBLX: Peak CCUs at 28.7M (strongest since Dec '25); JPM survey bullish on GTA VI/O18 opportunity
bullets.body: RBLX peak platform CCUs hit 28.7M Saturday (highest since Dec 2025). Steal An Egg peaked at 14.3M CCUs. JPM survey shows ~54% of Roblox users reduced spending in past 3 months but O18 users monetize ~50% higher vs U18; ~57% of global DAUs have age-verified. JPM maintains Neutral/$40 PT. EU KIDS Act (age 15+ independent accounts) poses moderate risk given RBLX's existing age-verification initiatives; Europe is ~21% of DAUs.

bullets.title: TSLA: Autonomous thesis intact but Optimus delayed; Cybercab modular; cash flow concern
bullets.body: Opco's Colin Langan expects Optimus ramp too aggressive with limited revenue before 2029 and ongoing perception stack challenges in adverse weather. Cybercab's modular architecture supports lower manufacturing costs. Tesla is auditing Chinese suppliers as Optimus commercialization nears. One researcher warns TSLA may be materially cash-flow negative this quarter and next unless Elon reduces compute bring-online plans. Hedgeye signals TSLA as bearish (buy $353, sell $373 range).

bullets.title: ORCL: Project Jupiter loans slide to stressed levels (89–91 cents); $18B NM datacenter debt under pressure
bullets.body: Oracle's ~$18B in loans backing its New Mexico (Project Jupiter) data center lease have slid into stressed territory, quoted at 89–91 cents on the dollar. One source describes the project as 'hopelessly mothballed.' Jefferies also notes Oracle debt pressures separately. No rating change disclosed.

bullets.title: HOOD: Hedgeye initiates with slight long bias; event contracts drove ~50% of revenue growth
bullets.body: Hedgeye is hosting a call Sept 23 on Robinhood, starting with a slight long bias. Event contracts drove nearly half of HOOD's revenue growth this year with continued runway. ~50% of revenue is still 'degenerate trading' with 90–100% incremental margins. Framework focuses on trading the cycle; current multiple assumes sustained good times. Crypto-related names including HOOD were up +5.1% pre-market on BTC +4.46%.
